title: Implement a Scheduled Data Retention Policy for the Data Warehouse
description: The MercuryLedger Data Warehouse is accumulating data indefinitely, leading to rising storage costs and degrading query performance. To manage this, a new feature is required to automatically purge old data from the warehouse based on a configurable retention period. This task involves adding the configuration for the retention period, implementing the core data purging logic, and scheduling this logic to run as a daily background job. This will test the agent's ability to work across configuration, data storage, and job scheduling layers of the application over multiple development sessions.

project_spec.name: MercuryLedger DW Insight
project_spec.description:
MercuryLedger DW Insight is an enterprise-grade data-warehouse solution written in C that equips medium-to-large corporations with a comprehensive view of their operational and financial performance. The project applies the MVVM paradigm to keep a strict separation between rich business rules (Model), real-time warehousing logic (View-Model) and multiple presentation surfaces (CLI dashboards, GTK desktop console, and REST/JSON adapters as ‘Views’). By combining Strategy, Observer, Pipeline, and Event-Streaming patterns, MercuryLedger ingests heterogeneous ERP, CRM and POS feeds into a governed Data Lake, executes high-throughput ETL pipelines with configurable data-quality stages, and produces batch/stream dashboards for executives and analysts.

Designed for a “hard” complexity level, the codebase spans 74 source/header files (~307 k tokens) and integrates advanced features such as rule-driven data validation, parallel batch orchestration, point-in-time error recovery, and smart scheduling. The business focus is reflected in pre-built financial KPI calculators, compliance checks (SOX/IFRS), and cost-center visualizations rendered directly from curated fact tables. Managers can subscribe to data-quality events, while DevOps teams monitor pipeline health through an Observer-based notification hub exposed via Prometheus exporters and desktop alerts.

MercuryLedger DW Insight not only highlights how MVVM can be achieved in a systems language like C, but also showcases how disciplined layering enables business stakeholders to evolve analytical requirements without touching low-level ingestion engines or storage back-ends.
dependencies: GLib/GTK 4 (UI layer for desktop dashboards – View)
protobuf-c (schema-first serialization between Model and ViewModel)
Apache Arrow C library (in-memory columnar data representation)
libpq (PostgreSQL driver for Data Lake persistence)
pthread / OpenMP (parallel ETL and batch jobs)
ZeroMQ (event streaming bus between pipeline stages)
Cairo + gnuplot pipes (data visualization charts in View)
zstd / lz4 (fast compression during data staging)
